- **Test image**: Microscope view (circular field) of a leaf. Visible: green leaf cells with clear cell wall boundaries, scattered clusters of raised brown/rust-colored pustules, fine white trichomes. Classic appearance of fungal pustules on leaf surface.

- **Soybean rust** (both refs): Shows small tan to brick-red spots on leaves — at microscopic level, these would correspond exactly to the brown uredinia (pustules) visible in the test image. Strong match.

- **Bacterial_Pustule** (ref): Shows darker purple-brown irregular lesions under magnification — different color and lesion character.

- **Downy_mildew** (ref): Shows yellow-green diffuse spots on upper surface — no match.

The brown raised pustule clusters on green leaf tissue, viewed through a microscope, is the hallmark of soybean rust uredinia. The rust description explicitly states "pustules forming on the lower leaf surface containing urediniospores" visible at 20x magnification — exactly what this image depicts.
